The FrogNet workflow

Source: vignettes/frognet-workflow.Rmd
frognet-workflow.Rmd

This vignette walks through the three stages of sheepdog as used in the FrogNet project (anurans of the Pantanal and Cerrado, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil). Paths, site names and the core species come from the FrogNet scripts of v1.2.0; settings marked “example” are illustrative. The FrogNet data are not distributed with the package, so the chunks that read them are not run; the last section runs on the example files shipped with the package.

library(sheepdog)

Stage 1a: clips to validate

Each site folder holds a BirdNET_SelectionTable.txt that concatenates the predictions of the custom classifier on every recording of the site. The recordings live on a NAS mapped as N:/ on Windows; on a Mac the same paths are remapped.

Check the selection first with simulate = TRUE: the manifest is written, but no audio is cut.

extract_validation_clips(
  data_dir   = "N:/Arara",
  output_dir = "N:/Arara/validation",
  n_top = 2,                     # top 2 per site x species x night x hour
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  hour_start = 17, hour_end = 2, # example: nights, small hours go to the
  alternate_days = TRUE,         #   night before; alternate nights
  target_total = 4000,           # clips per site, balanced among species
  balance_by_hour = TRUE,
  remap_from = "N:/", remap_to = "/Volumes/Arara/",
  simulate = TRUE
)

Then rerun with simulate = FALSE (the default). The clips go to validation/clips/<species>/, one zip per species to validation/packages/, and the map from each clip to its source to validation/clip_manifest.csv. A rerun skips the clips already cut.

The steps can also run one by one. select_clips() is pure: it returns the manifest without touching audio, which helps to try designs.

pred <- read_selection_tables("N:/Arara")
man  <- select_clips(pred, n_top = 2, target_total = 4000,
                     remap_from = "N:/", remap_to = "/Volumes/Arara/")
man  <- cut_clips(man, "N:/Arara/validation")
pack_clips(man, "N:/Arara/validation")

Estimating false-positive rates

The "top" design serves retraining and calibration, not the estimation of false-positive rates for occupancy models. For that, draw occasions at random among those with a detection, with the same threshold as the occupancy analysis (observation-confirmation design):

extract_validation_clips(
  "N:/Arara", "N:/Arara/validation_random",
  sampling_mode = "random_detections", threshold = 0.5,  # example values
  occasion_unit = "file", n_top = 1, target_total = 300,
  remap_from = "N:/", remap_to = "/Volumes/Arara/"
)

Every detection >= 0.5 of a drawn occasion is cut, and the manifest records inclusion_prob. See vignette("crywolf-integration") for the hand-off to occupancy models.

Stage 1b: after the review

The reviewers classify the clips in the review tab of the BirdNET GUI, which moves each clip into Positive/ or Negative/ subfolders.

# a FrogNet run cut by v1.2.0: the old manifest is read as well
post_validation(
  review_dir    = "E:/validacao_UEMS_meta4000/clipes",
  manifest_path = "E:/validacao_UEMS_meta4000/manifesto_clipes.csv",
  output_dir    = "E:/validacao_UEMS_meta4000/results",
  target_precision = 0.90, min_n = 15
)

This writes validation_by_clip.csv (the verdict of each clip), the precision by confidence bin, the lowest threshold reaching the target precision by species, the confirmed presence by night and the positive clips for retraining.

Stage 2: calibration

The reviewed clips of every site calibrate the confidence score into a probability of true detection. In FrogNet the manifest of site BEP came out as BEP2 and UEMS is abbreviated UEM, so site_map fixes the names.

dir_proj <- "~/Library/CloudStorage/Box-Box/Meus Artigos/2026-codigo FrogNet"
sites <- c("UEMS", "MIM", "ARA", "BAI", "XAR", "REF", "BEP")
res <- calibrate(
  validation_files  = file.path(dir_proj,
                                paste0("validacao_por_clipe_", sites, ".csv")),
  prediction_tables = c(
    UEM = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_UEMS.txt"),
    MIM = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_MIM.txt"),
    ARA = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_ARA.txt"),
    BAI = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_BAI.txt"),
    XAR = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_XAR.txt"),
    REF = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_REF.txt"),
    BEP = file.path(dir_proj, "BirdNET_SelectionTable_BEP.txt")),
  output_dir = "~/FrogNet_calibration",
  site_map   = c(BEP2 = "BEP", UEMS = "UEM"),
  p_min = 0.95, min_detections_night = 1
)
res$comparison

The candidate models go from a logistic regression on logit(confidence) to a binomial GLMM with random slopes by species and a site x species intercept. They are compared by 5-fold cross-validation stratified by site x species, and the best one is refitted to all the clips. Check the comparison and the calibration curves (calibration_curves.png) before using the probabilities. The calibrated detections of seven sites take about 700 MB, so keep output_dir outside a synced folder.

nightly_detection_history.csv gives, for each site x species x night, the number of detections with P(TP) >= p_min, and whether the night has a detection under the repetition rules k = 1, 2 and 3.

In FrogNet (2026), 6,304 reviewed clips (16 species x 7 sites) gave an AUC of 0.93 for the hierarchical model against 0.82 for the score alone, and about 3.15 million detections were scored.

Stage 3: community matrices

Ordinations (PCoA, NMDS, RDA) have no layer that absorbs false positives, so the entry rule is strict: at least two reliable detections in the night, only the core species (reliable calibration at every site), and site x month cells with at least five recorded nights.

build_community_matrices(
  "~/FrogNet_calibration/nightly_detection_history.csv",
  "~/FrogNet_community_matrices",
  core_species = c("boa_ran", "den_nan", "phy_alb", "rhi_dip", "sci_nas",
                   "lep_pod", "lep_fus", "pse_par", "pit_azu", "lys_lim"),
  k_min = 2, min_nights_month = 5
)

The six species with problematic calibration in FrogNet (tra_typ, boa_pun, den_min, sci_fuv, ade_dip, lep_ele) stay out; use them at most in a sensitivity analysis.

A runnable example

The example validation table shipped with the package comes from simulated data:

library(sheepdog)
val <- readr::read_csv(
  system.file("extdata", "validation_by_clip.csv", package = "sheepdog"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)
precision_by_bin(val, min_n = 3)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   site  species_folder bin       n_reviewed n_positive precision low_support
#>   <chr> <chr>          <fct>          <int>      <int>     <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1 ARA   boa_ran        [0.5,0.6)          3          1     0.333 FALSE      
#> 2 ARA   boa_ran        [0.6,0.7)          2          1     0.5   TRUE       
#> 3 ARA   boa_ran        [0.7,0.8)          3          3     1     FALSE      
#> 4 ARA   boa_ran        [0.9,1]            3          3     1     FALSE
nightly_presence(val)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   site  species_folder    night n_clips n_reviewed n_positive presence 
#>   <chr> <chr>             <dbl>   <int>      <int>      <int> <chr>    
#> 1 ARA   boa_ran        20220110       3          3          3 confirmed
#> 2 ARA   boa_ran        20220111       4          3          1 confirmed
#> 3 ARA   boa_ran        20220115       5          5          4 confirmed
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: max_confidence_positive <dbl>
